title: Git basics
description: Keep a history of your work: start a repository, save snapshots, see what changed.

exercises.task: Turn this folder into a git repository.
exercises.hint: git init starts a repository in the folder you're in. It makes a hidden .git folder.

exercises.task: Tell git your name, just for this project.
exercises.hint: git config user.name "Your Name" (without --global it only applies to this project)

exercises.task: And your email, for this project too.
Create a file called notes.txt containing the word hello.
Ask git what it thinks of this folder now.
exercises.hint: git status shows new, changed and staged files. It never changes anything.

exercises.task: Tell git to include notes.txt in the next snapshot.
exercises.hint: git add <file> 'stages' a file: it will go into the next commit.

exercises.task: Save a snapshot (a commit) with a short message.
Look at the history of this project.
exercises.hint: git log lists every commit, newest first. Press q to leave it.

exercises.task: Add the word world to the end of notes.txt.
exercises.hint: >> adds to the end of a file (one > would replace everything): echo world >> notes.txt

exercises.task: See exactly what changed since your last commit.
exercises.hint: git diff shows added lines with + and removed lines with -.

exercises.task: Save that change in a second commit.
exercises.hint: git commit -am "<message>" adds every changed file and commits in one go.

done: You just used git init, config, status, add, commit, log and diff: the everyday git loop.
